sf-business-registration.notes: Online-only filing at https://etaxstatement.sfgov.org/NewBusinessRegistration/application; then DocuSign e-signature sent to the business email - unsigned applications are deleted after 15 days. Then pay via etaxstatement.sfgov.org/OnlineBTPayment/ (some applications are reviewed before payment is allowed). Fields mapped from the paper PDF (rev 11/28/2022, header address Taxpayer Assistance, City Hall Room 140, #1 Dr. Carlton B. Goodlett Place, SF CA 94102) plus the NAICS question the online flow adds; the PDF is not listed on sftreasurer.org/find-form and the register page offers no mail/in-person filing, so don't use the PDF to file. 2026-27 fees: $55 (SF gross receipts $0-$100,000) up to $60,000 (>$200M) plus a $4 state fee; administrative offices pay $500-$35,000 based on payroll; First Year Free may waive initial fees. The page gives the registration deadline as 30 days after starting business, but its meta description says 15 days. It gives the renewal deadline as the last day of February, but the meta description says May. Certificate mailing time is stated as both 5-10 and 10-15 business days.

sf-dph-health-permit.notes: The application is online only and can be saved and resumed, but neither official page shows the portal URL or host (link targets weren't captured and sf.gov blocks direct fetch), so portal is left blank. The sfdph.org page still labels the online process 'Coming Soon!' and also tells applicants to bring documents to a Duty Officer appointment ((415) 252-3912). sf.gov treats the online application as live. Prerequisites: a location, SF business registration (BAN/LIN), at least one certified Food Safety Manager, and food handler cards for other food handlers. Apply at least 1 month before opening; sfdph says 6 weeks if construction or remodeling is involved. A change of ownership or entity type needs a new permit. Fees follow the EHB Fee Schedule, which I didn't read, so no amounts. For questions about supplemental documents, sf.gov names EnvHealth.DPH@sfdph.org as a contact, not as a place to submit. Closure forms are mailed to Environmental Health Branch, 49 South Van Ness Avenue, Suite 600, San Francisco, CA 94103.

sf-dph-plan-check.notes: Submitted in person with the DBI building permit at the Permit Center, 49 South Van Ness Avenue, DPH Counters 82/83. There's no destination key for in-person filing, so the address is recorded here. The form says submissions are accepted Monday-Friday 9-3, but the sf.gov guide lists Counter 83 hours as Monday, Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 7am-4pm and Wednesday 9am-4pm. The guide also says 'you may be able to submit your plans digitally' but names no channel. No fee amount appears on either page; staff confirm it at the appointment or after online submission. Pay online by invoice number, at Counter 83 (check, Visa, Mastercard), or by mail with a check payable to SFDPH, memo 'DPH Plan Check Fee for [project address]', to SFDPH, 49 South Van Ness Avenue, Suite 600, San Francisco, CA 94103. That mailing address is for fee payment only, not the application. Department contact: 415-252-3800. Required for submittal: this application, construction plans, and the fee payment. The form reminds applicants that new businesses or ownership changes must also apply for a DPH Health Permit to Operate at least 1 month before opening.

sf-formula-retail.notes: This is not a standalone filing. The affidavit 'must accompany any Building Permit Application' (or Permit Application) for alterations, new construction, commercial tenant improvements, change of use, or signage related to the use, so it goes wherever that permit is filed. No official page gives its own submission channel. The PDF lists 49 South Van Ness Avenue, Suite 1400, San Francisco, CA 94103 under 'APPLICATION PACKET' without saying it is a submission address, so I left mail out. Section 5 also contains declarations a)-e), acknowledgments signed under penalty of perjury that I didn't transcribe. The PDF is fillable, but browser-entered text isn't retained, so download it before filling. If Conditional Use Authorization is required, also file the 'Conditional Use for Formula Retail Authorization Supplemental' (sfplanning.org/resource/formula-retail-cua-supplemental). That triggers a Planning Commission hearing and possibly 30-day neighborhood notification. Contact: Planning counter 628.652.7300, pic@sfgov.org. The resource page was last updated 05/10/2026, but the form version is still 08.17.2020. I used the library's url; 'info' (sfplanning.org/permit/chain-stores-businesses) also resolves.

sf-sign.notes: ALERT: the library names 'Form 4 / Form 7 sign permit', but since Monday June 29, 2026 sign and awning permits (including Awning Amnesty legalization) are filed only through the PermitSF online portal. Form 4/7 is no longer used and paper applications are not accepted. The PermitSF portal host wasn't shown on any official page I could read, so portal is blank. Questions go to PermitSF@sfgov.org. Signature is set to 'typed' because the only filing route is the official online portal. I didn't see an attestation step. Fields come from the sf.gov step-by-step list of what the online form asks, not from the form itself. After filing, review results arrive by email with markups in Attachments; only the primary applicant can revise, by deleting the old attachment and uploading the new one via Update Application. Pay online in PermitSF or with cash/check at the Permit Center kiosk; no fee amounts were shown. A final inspection is required, plus an electrical inspection for illuminated signs. A Public Works street space permit may be needed. Most signs and awnings also have location-based zoning rules. The library url 'www.sf.gov/step-by-step--get-permit-install-sign-or-awning' is robots-blocked, so use the info URL sf.gov/step-by-step/get-permit-install-sign-or-awning. Agency: the page refers to DBI for electrical permits; PermitSF is the citywide permit portal.
